prd.name: Rust + Metal Terminal Engine
prd.overview: Replace SwiftTerm with a custom terminal engine: a Rust core (VT100/xterm emulator based on alacritty_terminal) renders through a Metal-backed UIView. The renderer targets 60 fps GPU-accelerated output with correct ANSI colour, clean scroll, and a Warp-style block-based input model with bottom-to-top expansion animation. The SSH transport, keyboard toolbar, direction pad, and app chrome are unchanged.
prd.why: SwiftTerm issues two bugs: monochrome output on the Metal path (ansi_colors_lost_with_metal) and scroll ghosting on the CoreGraphics path (scroll_drawing_ghosting). Choosing Metal over CoreGraphics trades colour for legibility - an unacceptable compromise for a terminal emulator. Beyond the bugs, the Warp-style block input model - where keystrokes are buffered locally and committed on Enter with an animated block rising from the input area into the terminal history - requires a level of renderer control that SwiftTerm does not expose.

requirement.name: Rust Terminal Core
requirement.description: A Rust static library (terminal_emu) wraps alacritty_terminal 0.24's parser and grid model and exposes it through a C FFI. Swift calls into it to feed bytes, read the terminal grid, and manage the Warp-style input block buffer.
requirement.rule: All VT100/xterm escape sequences parsed by alacritty_terminal - CSI, OSC, DCS, SGR (16/256/truecolor), DEC modes, mouse protocols, bracketed paste - are honoured.

The grid stores per-cell codepoint, foreground colour, background colour, and attribute flags (bold/italic/underline/inverse/dim/strikethrough). The grid is readable from Swift through a zero-copy FFI pointer.
Scrollback buffer is unbounded in memory, prunable to a configurable line count. Scroll position is exposed to the renderer.
term_feed(term, *const u8, len) accepts byte slices from Swift callers and returns a list of dirty line ranges for incremental repaint.
term_get_grid(term) returns a TerminalGrid struct with pointer to cell array, dimensions, cursor state, and dirty rect list, consumable from Swift without serialization.
A build.sh script invokes cargo build --release for aarch64-apple-ios and aarch64-apple-ios-sim. The resulting .a files are linked into BedTermKit via OTHER_LINKER_FLAGS.
A cbindgen.toml generates a terminal_emu.h header consumed by Swift via a module map or bridging header.

requirement.name: Metal Renderer
requirement.description: A UIView backed by MTKView draws the terminal grid at 60 fps using Metal shaders. The renderer composites per-cell glyph textures over ANSI-coloured backgrounds with attribute-aware blending. It uses incremental dirty-rect updates from the Rust core to avoid redrawing static regions.
requirement.rule: Glyphs are rasterised on the CPU via CoreText into a 2048×2048 RGBA8 MTLTexture atlas. The atlas is populated lazily: a glyph is rendered and uploaded only the first time its codepoint is encountered in the grid.
The fragment shader samples the glyph atlas and blends the result against the cell's ANSI foreground and background colours. Attribute flags (bold/italic/underline/inverse) are honoured in the blend.
ANSI 16-colour escapes map to the standard 4-bit palette, rendered with correct fg/bg colours in every frame.
ANSI 256-colour escapes render with the correct indexed colour.
SGR 38/48 true-colour escapes (ESC[38;2;R;G;Bm, ESC[48;2;R;G;Bm) render with the exact specified RGB values.
The cursor is drawn as a block, underline, or vertical bar (DECSCUSR) with a configurable blink cycle rendered in the Metal draw loop.
Only rows marked dirty by the Rust core are repainted in a given frame. A clean viewport (no output, no cursor blink) produces zero GPU work.
Scrolling the terminal history repaints the viewport cleanly on every frame: no doubled glyphs, no stale streaks, no scroll smearing.
The renderer respects Dynamic Type and switches between SF Mono and the system monospace font, re-rasterising the atlas on size change.
The ANSI 16-colour palette adapts to the iOS system appearance (Light/Dark) and updates live when the system appearance changes while the app is open.

requirement.name: Warp-Style Block Input
requirement.description: Instead of forwarding every keystroke directly to the PTY, user input is buffered locally in a block. On Enter, the block is committed: the full command text is sent to the remote PTY via bracketed paste (ESC[200~ … ESC[201~), locally echoed into the terminal grid, and an animated transition moves the block from the input area up into the terminal history.
requirement.rule: When the composer (R13) is presented, keystrokes are buffered in the Rust InputBuffer rather than sent to the PTY. The default passthrough mode is unchanged.
On Send, the buffer contents are dispatched to the remote PTY inside bracketed paste markers, and simultaneously fed into the local terminal emulator as local echo with a block-start sentinel.

Committed blocks animate from the input area upward into the terminal grid with a GPU-driven animation that expands the block's background from the input origin to its final grid position over ~300 ms.
The expansion uses an ease-in-out curve. The block border glow fades from full intensity to transparent over the animation duration.
Remote output arriving after the block commit is appended below the block in the grid, indistinguishable from normal command output.
When the block animation pushes content above the viewport, the terminal auto-scrolls to keep the block + new output visible.
Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Z, and Esc are never buffered: they pass through to the PTY immediately, even when the composer is presented.

requirement.name: No Regression on Existing Features
requirement.description: The replacement must not regress any rule marked ✅ in mvp.xml. The SSH transport, keyboard toolbar, direction pad, host-key TOFU, local-network prewarm, onboarding, app icon, and Lookin debug inspector are unchanged.
requirement.rule: R1 (SSH Connection): all rules still pass.
R2 (Terminal Display): all rules pass with ANSI colours now correct.
R3 (Special Keys Toolbar): all rules still pass.
R4 (Ctrl Combination Mode): all rules still pass.
R5 (Basic Terminal UX): copy/paste/scroll/prompt-anchor/font/dark-mode all pass.
R6 (Host Key TOFU): unchanged.
R7 (Local Network Permission): unchanged.
R8 (App Icon): unchanged.
R9 (System Appearance): now passes with live palette switching.
R10 (Onboarding): unchanged.
R11 (Direction Pad): unchanged.
R12 (Lookin): unchanged. The MTKView is inspectable.
R13 (Composer): reimplemented as the Warp-style InputBuffer UI.
R14 (Voice Input): dictation inserts into the InputBuffer, not directly to PTY.

requirement.name: Warp-Style Input Composer UI
requirement.description: The composer UI replaces the R13 multiline input area with a Warp-style input block. Visually: - A monospace editing area sits below the terminal view, styled with Liquid Glass - The editing area is a single growing block, not a traditional text view - Each committed block appears in the terminal with a subtle left-border accent (like Warp's command blocks) and a timestamp
requirement.rule: The composer is a monospace text area using the same font and size as the terminal, with no autocorrect/autocapitalisation/smart punctuation.
Committed blocks in the terminal history have a 2px left-border accent (blue for commands, green for successful exit, red for non-zero exit) that persists across scrollback.
Each committed block shows a faint timestamp above the block's first line in the terminal.
Blocks whose output exceeds one viewport height collapse to a summary line ("N lines hidden") with a tap-to-expand affordance.

issue.title: Three-phase delivery
issue.description: Phase 1: Rust core + basic Metal renderer achieving feature parity with SwiftTerm (but with colour and scroll fixed). Input remains PTY-passthrough. Phase 2: Warp-style InputBuffer + composer UI + block commit flow. Phase 3: Block animation, collapse, accent borders, timestamp polish.

issue.title: alacritty_terminal iOS compatibility
issue.description: alacritty_terminal 0.24 has not been tested on iOS. Its macOS build may rely on POSIX APIs not available on iOS. A compatibility audit is needed before Phase 1 begins. Fallback: the pure-Rust vt100 crate which is known to build for iOS.

issue.title: Glyph atlas memory budget
issue.description: A 2048×2048 RGBA8 atlas is 16 MB. CJK character sets have 20,000+ glyphs which exceeds one atlas. A multi-atlas or LRU eviction strategy may be needed. Profile with real CJK usage before committing to a size.

issue.title: Local echo vs remote echo race
issue.description: When a block is committed, the local echo inserts the command text into the terminal grid immediately. If the remote shell echoes the same text (common in canonical/cooked mode), the command text appears twice. Mitigation: set the PTY to raw mode (-echo) on connect, or suppress remote echo for the first N bytes after commit.

bug.current: With the Metal renderer toggle ON, tapping on the terminal viewport does NOT bring up the system soft keyboard. The view conforms to UIKeyInput and a tap-gesture recogniser calls becomeFirstResponder(), but the iOS keyboard never appears. Input from a hardware/simulator keyboard still flows through (UIKeyInput.insertText receives the bytes), but a real iPhone user with no hardware keyboard has no way to type into the terminal.
bug.expected: A single tap on the terminal viewport in the Metal path should present the iOS system keyboard, the same way it does on the SwiftTerm path. Either canBecomeFirstResponder isn't being honoured by MTKView, or another responder (the long-press selection recogniser, the focus-tap recogniser itself) is consuming the tap before the keyboard presents, or MTKView refuses to present a keyboard without an explicit inputView.
bug.steps: 1. Build and run with Metal toggle ON. Connect to a host. 2. Tap once on the terminal viewport. 3. Observe: nothing happens — the toolbar stays at the bottom, no soft keyboard slides in. Compared to SwiftTerm toggle OFF, where the same tap presents the keyboard above the toolbar.

bug.current: On the first command typed after connecting via the Metal renderer, the typed echo line renders with several characters missing or visibly corrupted (e.g. typing "echo metal_input_test" renders as roughly "ec' _test", with large gaps between fragments). The shell receives every byte correctly — running the command works, and its output ("metal_input_test") renders cleanly on the next line. Subsequent commands typed in the same session render their echo lines correctly.
bug.expected: Every cell that TerminalCore.snapshot() reports as non-blank must appear on screen, regardless of whether it's the first or hundredth line in the session. The first-paint of a freshly-echoed line should render the same as any later paint.
bug.steps: 1. Build and run with Metal toggle ON. Connect to a host. 2. With a hardware/simulator keyboard attached, type "echo metal_input_test". 3. Press Return. 4. Observe: the typed command line ("yi.jiang:~/ $ echo metal_input_test") renders with gaps — many characters missing visually even though the shell echoed them. The output line ("metal_input_test") renders cleanly, and subsequent commands typed in the same session render their echo lines correctly.

bug.current: With the Metal renderer toggle ON, the shell's first prompt and any short transcript renders pinned to the top of the terminal viewport while the rest of the viewport stays black. After connecting to an SSH host, the screen shows "Last login: …" on row 0 and "yi.jiang:~/ $" on row 1, then a large black gap down to the toolbar — instead of the prompt sitting on the row just above the toolbar with empty space above it.
bug.expected: Per R5.prompt_anchored_bottom: when the transcript is shorter than the viewport, the active prompt line is anchored to the bottom edge of the terminal viewport (just above the special-keys toolbar) and any empty space sits above it. The Metal renderer must apply the same bottom-anchor behaviour the SwiftTerm path does via TerminalHostView.Coordinator.scheduleBottomAnchorPass — pad the visible grid with blank lines above the prompt so the cursor lands on the bottom row of the viewport.
bug.steps: 1. Launch the app, enable the Debug → Metal renderer (experimental) toggle. 2. Tap Connect to open an SSH session. 3. Wait for the shell prompt to appear. 4. Observe: the "Last login" line and the prompt sit on rows 0–1 of the viewport; the bottom ~90% of the terminal area is empty black. The cursor is at top, not above the toolbar.

bug.current: With the debug toggle useMetalRenderer turned ON, the terminal view is rendered by TerminalMetalUIView but the system keyboard's keystrokes never reach the remote PTY. Typing produces no echo and no command execution; only the special-keys toolbar (ESC/CTRL/TAB, dpad) and the composer can send bytes to the host.
bug.expected: With the Metal renderer active, typing on the system keyboard should send each keystroke to the remote PTY exactly as the SwiftTerm path does today — including ordinary characters, Return, Backspace, and hardware-keyboard key commands. The first-responder hand-off driven by yieldFirstResponder in the host view should make the terminal view accept input when the composer is not open.
bug.steps: 1. Build and install the app on the simulator with the Metal toggle off (default SwiftTerm path). 2. Open the Connection screen and enable the new "Debug → Metal renderer (experimental)" toggle. 3. Connect to any SSH host. The remote prompt renders correctly. 4. Tap the terminal view to bring up the system keyboard. 5. Type any character on the keyboard. 6. Observe: no character echoes in the terminal, no shell activity, no bytes leave the device. The toolbar's ESC/CTRL/TAB still work; the composer's Send still works. Only direct keyboard typing into the terminal view is dropped.

bug.current: With the Metal renderer toggle ON, the iOS system keyboard's globe / language-switch key has no effect when focus is in the terminal view. The user cannot switch to a non-English input method (e.g. Pinyin, Japanese Romaji, Korean 2-set) to type CJK input. Under the SwiftTerm path, the same keyboard correctly cycles through installed input modes.
bug.expected: The Metal terminal view should accept every installed iOS keyboard language. Tapping the globe key (or long-pressing it) should cycle through input modes the same way it does in any standard text field, and the selected IME's marked-text / composition UI should appear over the terminal viewport. Committed text from the IME should be fed into the PTY as UTF-8 bytes.
bug.steps: 1. In iOS Settings → General → Keyboard, add a non-English keyboard (e.g. Chinese — Simplified, Pinyin). 2. Build and run with the Metal toggle ON. Connect to a host. 3. Bring up the soft keyboard on the terminal view. 4. Tap the globe key to switch input language. 5. Observe: the keyboard does not switch language, or the globe key is unresponsive. The current input mode remains English. Toggle Metal OFF and repeat — SwiftTerm switches input modes normally.

bug.current: With the Metal renderer toggle ON, CJK characters (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) are not rendered in the terminal viewport. Output containing CJK codepoints either shows as blank cells, tofu boxes, or garbled glyphs — even though the Rust core's grid correctly stores the codepoints (the same session under SwiftTerm renders the characters correctly).
bug.expected: Every codepoint stored in the terminal grid should be rasterised into the Metal glyph atlas on first encounter and rendered with the correct shape, including the full CJK Unified Ideographs range and Hiragana/Katakana/Hangul blocks. Wide (double-width) CJK glyphs should occupy two cells horizontally without clipping or overlap with neighbouring cells.
bug.steps: 1. Build and run with Metal toggle ON. Connect to a host. 2. At the prompt, run a command that prints CJK text, e.g. echo "你好 こんにちは 안녕". 3. Observe: the CJK characters do not appear correctly in the Metal viewport — blank cells, tofu, or garbled output. Toggle Metal OFF and repeat: SwiftTerm renders the same string correctly.

bug.current:
With the Metal renderer toggle ON, the painted grid lags the terminal state by exactly one input event:
After pressing Return, the next prompt line (e.g. yi.jiang:fix-saved-connections/) is blank but the cursor sits at the correct column where the prompt's end would be. The prompt only fills in after the next keystroke arrives.
Typing hello renders as hell with the cursor one cell to the right of hell — the last typed glyph (o) is missing until another key is pressed, which paints the o and then leaves the new last glyph missing.
The cursor position always reflects the latest state, but the cell at cursor - 1 (or the entire row just produced by Return) is the previous state. The Rust core has the correct bytes — it's the Metal paint that runs against the pre-update grid.
bug.expected: Every byte fed to term_feed must be reflected in the very next frame, not the frame after. After pressing Return, the new prompt line should paint together with the cursor. After typing a character, that character should paint in the same frame as the cursor advancing past it.
bug.steps: 1. Build and run with Metal toggle ON. Connect to a host. 2. At the prompt, press Return. 3. Observe: the new prompt row is empty, but the cursor sits where the end of the prompt should be. 4. Type any single key; the previously-missing prompt now appears, and the new key's glyph is itself missing one cell behind the cursor. 5. Type hello; observe the rendered text is hell with a one-cell gap before the cursor.
